direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt requires a pure ESM Node.js migration in /output with .mjs files, manual argparse-compatible argv parsing, no external modules, and black-box parity with the executable.
Parallel cell metadata reports actual parallel use, five subagents, agent timeout, empty quality result of 0/160, and solution_passed false.
Current completed official evaluation supersedes aggregate status and records process timeout, empty artifact validation, and 0/160 passing evaluator samples.
Evaluation summary confirms the official Docker evaluator completed, marked solution_passed false, and recorded 0 passed samples out of 160.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server event stream contains transport records only and contributes no semantic task actions to the projected review ledger.
Session index is a transport-only source identifying the parallel Kimi session and has no projected semantic work events.
Explorer agent-0 characterized fragment behavior through many executable probes, bytecode extraction, and a final technical report without modifying deliverables.
Explorer agent-1 characterized URL parsing, normalization, scheme and netloc rules, including bundled furl version and edge-case probes.
Explorer agent-2 characterized argparse-compatible CLI behavior, help output, missing arguments, duplicate options, empty values, and option-like values.
Explorer agent-3 characterized output string conversion and percent-encoding behavior, including Unicode, percent escapes, newlines, and query formatting.
Implementation child received the post-investigation implementation task, performed more probes and todo setup, but was cancelled before writing or returning code.
Parent probed a few cases, launched a four-agent investigation swarm, consumed the aggregate report, then delegated implementation to a child that failed after cancellation.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt is byte-identical to the parallel prompt and requires the same pure ESM Node.js migration, argv behavior, and executable-based black-box validation.
Serial cell metadata reports no parallel use, no subagents, an artifact present, agent timeout, and quality of 122/160 with solution_passed false.
Current completed official evaluation records the submitted artifact files and 122/160 passing evaluator samples despite a timeout and failed final solution flag.
Evaluation summary confirms the official Docker evaluator completed, marked solution_passed false, and recorded 122 passed samples out of 160.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server event stream contains transport records only and no projected semantic work events for the serial run.
Session index is a transport-only source identifying the serial Kimi session and has no projected semantic work events.
Single serial actor probed the executable, inferred fragment and URL rules, wrote ESM modules and an entry file, created a differential test script, and found one remaining mismatch before timeout.

parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the source program, pure Node.js ESM requirement, .mjs suffixes, no npm dependencies, manual argv parsing, and character-for-character output parity with the executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent first created a four-agent investigation swarm covering fragments, URL normalization, CLI parsing, and output encoding, then later assigned the whole implementation and verification job to one additional child.
parallel.implementation: The exploration agents produced detailed observations, but the implementation child repeated additional probes and did not reach code-writing events before cancellation.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No implemented files were incorporated into the official artifact; artifact validation reported an empty file list rather than /output/test12.mjs and libraries.
parallel.verification: The parallel run performed many oracle probes in child and parent contexts, but no integrated Node implementation test was completed because the implementation stage never produced files.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The active implementation child was cancelled before returning a finished implementation, the run timed out, and the official evaluator saw no submitted artifact, giving 0/160.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same ESM, .mjs, no-dependency, manual argv, and output-parity requirements from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned probing, implementation, test creation, and final artifact production without delegating work to subagents.
serial.implementation: The serial actor wrote /output/lib modules for encoding, path, query, fragment, URL splitting, furl behavior, argparse handling, and the /output/test12.mjs entry point.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact validation listed test12.mjs, difftest.sh, and seven library modules under lib, so a deliverable tree was available for evaluation.
serial.verification: The serial actor created and ran a broad differential test script; it found one mismatch on leading-whitespace URLs and then timed out while investigating it.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The implementation was incomplete because one known differential mismatch remained and the official evaluator passed only 122/160 samples, but the run still delivered partial code.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the migration requirements and decomposed behavior discovery around the executable and furl semantics.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt requirements and used the executable as the oracle while implementing in ESM files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement understanding was broadly similar; the material difference was not prompt comprehension but when implementation work began and whether deliverables were written.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split the first phase into four investigation subagents and deferred the full implementation to a later coder child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept probing, coding, and testing under one local owner and used todos rather than delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel separated investigation from production work, while serial interleaved analysis with file creation and kept one owner for the full path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs were scoped to research reports first; the later implementation brief contained summarized established behavior but arrived after the investigation phase.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial accumulated its own observations directly in the same trajectory that wrote the implementation modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No cross-agent interface contract was needed in serial, while parallel had to transfer a large behavior summary into a late implementation child.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implementation remained in the late child probing phase and no code-writing event appears before cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote encoding, path, query, fragment, urlsplit, furl, argparse, and entry modules before running differential tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial reached concrete code generation; parallel did not deliver any implementation into the evaluated artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited on a late implementation child and received a stopped-before-finished error rather than a usable child result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join and kept its intermediate findings in the same actor context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel depended on a child result that never finalized, whereas serial had direct access to its own files and test output.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel status shows artifact validation copied an empty directory and found no expected entry file.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial status shows artifact validation found test12.mjs, difftest.sh, and library files under lib.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The serial run left a coherent artifact tree for evaluation; parallel left no submitted implementation to integrate or run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had oracle probes but no completed Node implementation verification or acceptance loop.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran a generated differential test and observed one remaining mismatch after 69 passing probe cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial at least verified an implemented artifact and exposed a specific defect; parallel never reached an implemented artifact test.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after the late implementation child was cancelled, and no artifact files were available at closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but only after it had written an implementation and run a differential test with one mismatch.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the run budget, but serial spent enough of it on production work to leave partial passing output; parallel consumed it before deliverable creation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official relation is both_fail because both current completed evaluations set solution_passed false. The practical score gap is nevertheless large: parallel produced an empty artifact and 0/160, while serial produced ESM files and a partial implementation that passed 122/160. The best-supported contributor is the parallel run's investigation-first workflow, which delayed implementation until the child was cancelled before delivering code.
parallel_contributors: Four investigation subagents were launched and completed before any implementation owner began writing code.
The later implementation child was cancelled before returning a finished result, leaving the official artifact empty.
serial_contributors: The single serial actor wrote the ESM library and entry files before timeout.
The serial actor ran a differential test and identified a remaining leading-whitespace mismatch before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial still had an ordinary implementation defect after its differential test, which is consistent with 122/160 rather than a full pass.
Parallel had no delivered implementation to expose ordinary coding defects in the evaluator.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an official pass/fail discordance or exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: The parallel parent explicitly assigned implementation to agent-4; the problem is late/cancelled execution, not absence of an implementation owner.
No separately implemented components were completed and left for reconciliation, so there was no unowned integration object.
The late implementation child was responsible for creating the /output deliverable; assembly did not go unassigned as a separate object.
The parent coordinated the investigation-to-implementation transition; the failure was the serial investigation phase consuming the delivery window, not an ownerless pipeline.
There was not one mandatory serial preflight gate; the parent ran a multi-agent investigation phase and then a separate implementation child.
The parent waited for overlapping investigators and additional probes before assigning implementation, leaving the implementation child to start too late and be cancelled before deliverable creation.
candidates.realized_consequence: Implementation started only after the investigation phase and was cancelled before code was returned, causing an empty official artifact and 0/160 evaluator samples.
candidates.near_match_reason: The same facts include high child use and timeout, but the clearest boundary is that investigation was completed as a first phase before production work began.

candidates.reason: The indispensable implementation path was delayed by an investigation-first plan, which is captured by Serial Investigation rather than a generic capacity starvation label.
Although the run used a four-agent exploration fan-out and timed out, the retained episode is the serial investigation phase; the fan-out budget symptom is not independent.
Agent-4 received a broad implementation brief, but its cancellation is part of the same delayed implementation chain and is not retained as a separate oversized-scope episode.

The executed implementation child was briefed with the core source, ESM constraints, no-dependency rule, argparse requirement, and established behavior, so no known task requirement omission is proven.
No multiple completed component implementations were expected to interoperate; the only production owner was the late implementation child.
The parent had the investigation result and provided a substantive behavior summary to the implementation child; no specific known fact is shown disappearing in transfer.
The AgentSwarm result was large, but the parent consumed it into an implementation brief; the adverse consequence is better explained by the investigation-first schedule than by unreadable bulk.
No child or parent action is shown relying on superseded workspace or requirement state after a newer state was available.
The explorer reports had nuances but no unadjudicated incompatible contract that blocked or corrupted integration is directly evidenced.
The parallel parent did not present the whole task as complete; the run ended by cancellation and empty artifact validation instead.
No replacement or retry child repeated the same work without inherited findings; the implementation child was the first production attempt.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: Agent-4 was explicitly cancelled, but this is the terminal symptom of the retained investigation-before-implementation episode, so it is not retained as a separate timing label.
No complete, directly promotable implementation candidate or compatible component set existed before closure; the implementation child had not returned code.
No parallel implementation change was merged after an integrated verification step, because no implementation was produced for the parent to merge.
The delegated implementation was not completed or retrievable; the parent received a stopped-before-finished error rather than ignoring a completed implementation.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding trapped below the parent; the child that failed was the implementation child.
The parent was cancelled as the run timed out immediately after the child failed, so there is no distinct post-failure decision point where it ignored takeover.
The implementation child never produced a completed result available for the parent to inspect, use, or reject.
The wait ended in the same late implementation cancellation chain; there is no separate evidence that available progress was inspectable and ignored.
No concurrent actors produced competing implementations in different files for overlapping behavior.
No two live parallel agents edited the same source or configuration file with observed reconciliation.
No parallel actor replaced another actor's non-entry source file; the implementation child did not reach source writes.
No agent replaced the required executable, entry source, or submitted artifact while another actor owned it.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced current final outputs from another actor.
Multiple live parallel agents did not write shared implementation workspace files in a way that caused unstable state or provenance confusion.
Exploratory temporary files were not shown being consumed by another actor as stable input or reference environment.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel parent completed a multi-agent investigation phase before assigning implementation, and the late implementation child was cancelled before producing a deliverable.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The official parallel artifact was empty and the evaluator had no implementation to score, resulting in 0/160 passed samples.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The same episode includes fan-out and timeout evidence, but the distinctive coordination error is that all investigation ran before productive implementation.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Early Child Termination was not retained separately because the cancellation was the downstream end of the same late implementation episode.
Fan-out Budget Exhaustion and Oversized Child Task were not retained separately because they share the same delayed implementation consequence and corrective action.
Blind Timeout Wait and No Failure Takeover were rejected because there was no distinct available result or post-failure takeover point beyond the same cancellation chain.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were considered; only Serial Investigation cleared the paired retention gate.
